relevance_note: The paper reports two children with TNFAIP3 variants: 'Herein, we report two children with the primary presentation of HLH, with a mutation in TNFAIP3'.
method_note: Read the whole paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON from values I typed and checked every span verbatim against the Markdown. No table was transcribed by script. Individuals: 'Patient one' and 'Patient two' are the authors' own cases (labels from the section headings; Table 3 calls them 'Our patient N. 1' and 'Our patient N. 2'). Table 3 also lists two previously published patients, recorded with the table's Number column as label: '1' (Li et al. [29], also described in the Discussion text) and '2' (Takagi et al [9], also described in the text). The Discussion summarises three previously published patients of Zhang et al. [25], recorded as 'One patient', 'The second patient' and 'The third patient' (no variant, sex or age given; the paper does not explicitly label them HA20, so disease_label is 'not reported'). is_proband left null for all: the paper never uses 'proband'/'index case' and reports two unrelated patients. Patient one: age at genetic (HA20) diagnosis recorded as 2 years 4 months; HLH was diagnosed at presentation at 4 months; age at last evaluation and age at death not stated. Zygosity of p.T129M not stated (only 'a mutation'), so 'not reported'. Patient two: age at report given only as '4 years have passed since the first presentation' (iso left null); 6q23.3 is a cytoband, so genomic coordinates null; SIFT/PolyPhen-2/CADD are in silico, not functional assays, so they are in pathogenicity, not functional evidence. Takagi patient: the paper says 'de novo mutation' but gives no parental testing statement, so inheritance 'not reported' under rule 8. Li patient: the text prints 'c.259C > T (p.R87X) ... (RS: NM_006290)' while Table 3 prints 'c.C259T, p.R87X'; recorded the text form. Checklist choices: a single or prolonged 'fever' was not counted as 'recurrent fever' (only 'intermittent fever' was); HLH-related pancytopenia was not counted as 'cytopenia (autoimmune)'; hepatosplenomegaly was not counted as lymphoproliferation; Patient one's cerebral hemorrhage with coma was counted as CNS involvement; the general statement that 'Our patients did not have any symptoms of Behcet’s-like or other autoimmune disorders' was recorded as a phenotypic_features row but not used to exclude specific checklist items; Patient one's 'No other abnormality was found' and Table 3 '-' cells were not used to exclude anything. Contradictions/inconsistencies in the paper: (1) Patient two's variant is described as 'a proline to leucine amino acid change (p. L275P)', but p.L275P denotes leucine to proline. (2) Patient one: the case text says 'the HLH criteria were met according to HLH protocol 2004', the Discussion says 'it might be suggested that all five HLH criteria were not met in the first patient'. (3) Patient one: text says 'normal ESR, CRP, and procalcitonin levels' but Table 1 gives ESR 11 (0-10), CRP 6 (<6) and procalcitonin 0.2 (<0.1); recorded as excluded per the text with the values in severity_or_detail. (4) Patient two: 'the coagulation profile was normal, except for thrombocytopenia' although fibrinogen was 93* and hypofibrinogenemia is listed. (5) Patient two: 'familial HLH (FHL) was confirmed' before genetic testing, although the Discussion describes FHL as autosomal recessive with specific genes. (6) Patient two: leukocytosis and thrombocytosis are said to have resolved after 2 months of etanercept, but no time point with leukocytosis/thrombocytosis is shown (Table 2 values at 4 weeks are normal). (7) Background says 'we present a case of genetically confirmed HA20' though two cases are reported. (8) Takagi patient: text says 'pancytopenia', Table 3 lists 'thrombocytopenia'; both recorded.
